source.title: Every Component is a Lookup: Token Attribution and Composition from a Single Decomposition
source.authors: Po-Kai Chen; Niki van Stein; A. Plaat

page_placements.theme: Ablation compared with retraining and observational estimates: ablation can overstate as well as understate

record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses the distinction between contribution and causal effect and reports communication-knockout results, but does not test whether downstream components compensate for an ablation.
record.gate_note: The paper removes a component's residual contribution from downstream attention or MLP LayerNorm inputs and reports correlations between interaction scores and knockout perplexity effects. These results do not measure downstream output changes or restoration, so they do not test any listed version. The correlation results are recorded as related findings under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The study validates an observational attribution graph (UNPACK) against communication-specific knockouts, path-patched circuits and input flipping. It never measures whether downstream components compensate after an ablation: no restoration, direct-versus-total effect or erasure measure appears. It does not cite the Hydra or self-repair papers. Its only related point is a general contrast between contribution and causal necessity at layer 0, which is not self-repair. So it neither tests nor uses the claim (T6); 'discusses' is kept only loosely, for that contrast.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is largely correct. The authors argue that two assumptions suffice for all three readouts: a shared key-value form and an additive residual stream. Each readout passes an established check: knockout prediction, recovery of the IOI and greater-than circuits, and input-flipping faithfulness. They also find that contribution diverges from causal effect at layer 0, where components behave like a prompt-independent bias. Contribution complements intervention rather than replacing it.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses a single-forward-pass attribution graph and communication-specific knockouts to validate interaction scores; it does not implement or reproduce a self-repair ablation method.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that knockout-score correlations vary by model scale and channel; the attention channel is noisier than the MLP channel.

fits_no_version.finding: Within-layer Spearman correlation between interaction score and communication-knockout Δppl: 0.72–0.86 for attention and 0.86–0.96 for MLP, across Pythia-deduped 160M–6.9B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Observational key-side interaction scores rank the perplexity effects of communication-specific knockouts across Pythia-deduped scales.

fits_no_version.finding: Layer-0 components receive high credit on both IOI prompts and ABC controls. Circuit components found by path patching lose 30–70 coverage points when the task is removed.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Observational contribution diverges from causal relevance mainly through prompt-independent, bias-like early components.

record.problems: The knockout results report aggregate score-to-Δppl correlations, not downstream recovery or direct-versus-total effects. The described knockout evaluation uses 200 held-out Pile sentences and selects a subset of components per source layer.

untested.parts: Whole version: no layer ablation followed by measurement of later-layer compensation or output restoration.
Whole version: no late-MLP erasure of the top token, and no change in erasure after earlier ablation.
Whole version: no single-head ablation comparing direct effect with total effect on general text.
Whole version: no per-prompt compensation distribution and no overcorrection measure.
Whole version: backup heads, copy suppression, LayerNorm rescaling and anti-erasure neurons are not examined as repair mechanisms.
Whole version: only residual-vector subtraction knockouts are used, with no comparison of ablation types for self-repair.
Whole version: the gap between contribution and causal effect is attributed to layer-0 bias-like components, not to self-repair distorting ablation scores.

record.verdict_notes: All rows are correctly unlinked (versions 'none', cannot_determine). Interaction scores are aggregated over 1,000 Pile sentences, while Δppl is measured on 200 held-out sentences, with 5 components selected per source layer. The knockouts subtract a component's clean residual vector from downstream LayerNorm inputs. This is a channel ablation, but its downstream recovery is never quantified. Nothing in the text bears on any self-repair version.

versions.untested_parts: Layer ablation followed by compensation in later attention layers and restoration of the original output.
Late-MLP downregulation of the maximum-likelihood token and its change after earlier ablation.
Head-level compensation on the full distribution across general text, model families, and sizes.
Prompt-level variation, average compensation, and overcorrection.
The named self-repair mechanisms listed in this version.
Self-repair under mean or resample ablations versus zero ablation.
Whether self-repair causes ablation-based importance scores to misstate component function.

relation.reason: The contribution-versus-causal-effect discussion is relevant to attribution, but the study neither tests nor uses self-repair.

tranche.reason: Communication-knockout correlations and observational credit do not measure downstream compensation, restoration, or changes in erasure after ablation.

source_check.notes: Within-layer correlations are means of per-source-layer correlations. The supplied text is v3, dated 24 September 2026, with a different subtitle from the check-pack title.

statements.correction: Appendix C, Table 5: Pythia-deduped 160M–6.9B; mean per-source-layer Spearman correlations 0.72–0.86 attention, 0.86–0.96 MLP. Figure 3: GPT-2 small; claimed components lose 30–70 coverage points at layers 2–6 and about 15 at layers 7–8; matched ABC controls restricted to prompts where A is not the top prediction. Layer-0 components retain high credit and coverage across IOI and ABC prompts.
statements.problem: The correlation ranges are correct, but the coverage-drop summary omits its layer restriction and the smaller drops at later layers. That experiment uses GPT-2 small.
